content:
- Applied improve-code-boundaries smell 10 in src/process/worker.rs by removing the one-caller inbox-drain helper and inlining that behavior into step_once.
- Added a step_once behavior test proving only the latest queued request is rejected when the worker is busy; make lint and make test both passed afterward.
- Committed as 2e92cc0 and pushed to origin/master, then ran bash .ralph/task_switch.sh; current task summaries were updated and the script again printed a harmless missing .ralph/current_task.txt removal message. If resuming later, note there are still unrelated pre-existing dirty files plus new post-switch .ralph changes in the worktree.

- Read prior progress and loaded the improve-code-boundaries skill instructions.
- Confirmed there are pending found_smells files, so this run must use one of those first.
- Checked git status and Makefile; make test uses cargo nextest, so it is compatible with the repo rule against cargo test.

- Chose the found smell in src/ha/process_dispatch.rs rather than touching the user's existing dirty files.
- The boundary issue is the unused RuntimeConfig threaded into dispatch_process_action from ha/worker; this matches smell 3 exactly.
- Next: remove that contaminated argument, update the single caller, validate, then delete the processed found_smell file.
